newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt ends weaker on poor Australian performance.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt ends weaker on poor Australian performance.

* Weak Australian debt market drags NZ yields up at close
* Volumes better than those of late, but still light
* RBNZ's econ forecasts the next driver - dealer
New Zealand debt ended on a weak note on Thursday, with yields dragged higher by a poor performance from Australian bonds.
News of the death of China's paramount leader, Deng Xiaoping, had no impact on the market.
A growing picture of a healthier economy weighed on the Australian market, and yields soon extended their weaker trend as technical selling pushed them through support levels.
Local dealers said the Australian developments had finally given the market something to focus on. Flows had been heavier than in recent days but were still "hardly high".
"Volumes have been pretty inconsistent and patchy over the last few weeks now, and today wasn't an awful lot different," one dealer said.
The mid and long bonds finished around three basis points weaker, while the 90-day bank bills remained trapped in a tight range. They finished four basis points weaker at 7.42 percent.

Some dealers expect Friday's Labour Cost Index to provide a bit of direction, but others say the market has been discounting recent economic indicators and they see the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's economic forecasts, due March 13, as the next major trigger.

"I don't think people are actually carrying around positions in this market at all, and therefore even if the Labour Cost Index is quite a lot different from expectations, if people actually haven't got anything they need to do on the back of it, then there's not alot of volatility," one dealer said. -------------------------(SPREADS)------------------------------
